gaps.sentence: The novel ___ (write) in under three months.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive (was/were + past participle): was written. The writer is not mentioned.

gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
gaps.hint: passive of a verb with two objects
gaps.explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.

gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: A new ring road ___ (construct) around the city at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' requires present continuous passive: is being + constructed.

gaps.sentence: The tickets ___ at the door from seven o'clock.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: can be + collected. The tickets are collected by the buyers.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.
